attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. He states the chain himself.

semantics.note: The wording is firm. The antecedent 'if OpenAI fails' is kept, and the chain OpenAI→CoreWeave→NVIDIA is preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'fails' as business failure is the plain, ordinary reading. The contract scores the chain only after the antecedent occurs, which is fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of 2026-10-27 shows ongoing commercial activity. It shows no failure, so it does not test the chain.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet contains no OpenAI business failure by the cutoff, so the antecedent has not occurred and the claim cannot be scored. Nothing tests the CoreWeave or NVIDIA links.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, written in the first person.

semantics.note: 'Isn't realistic… even in my most optimistic frame' is firm pessimism, so it is a scorable forecast that they can't build the capacity. The drafter's 'unlikely' modality label understates this. No horizon is given.

contract.note: Limiting scope to the Abilene and Core Scientific/CoreWeave buildouts discussed in the post is reasonable. Requiring full delivery, or an irreversible failure, to resolve is fair given that no threshold or deadline was stated.

evidence.note: Crusoe disclosure: the first two Abilene buildings were energized with early workloads running. This is only an initial phase, not the full expansion.
June 2026 Crusoe disclosure: 2 buildings operational and 6 still under construction. The campus is not complete, and there is no failure.
Core Scientific Q2 2026: 437 MW billing. It is not mapped to OpenAI's needs or to completion of the expansion.

reviews.rationale: Partial delivery by both builders is real counterweight, but by the cutoff the evidence shows neither completed, accepted expansion capacity nor an irreversible failure to deliver. Under the contract this is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assessment, which he supports with cited reporting.

semantics.note: An observation of schedule slippage. 'Appears' is evidential but is backed by specific milestones, so it is treated as a checkable observation rather than a probability hedge.

contract.note: Comparing the Q1 2025 GPU target with spring 2025 status follows the speaker's own context. The contract rightly separates GPU deployment from building occupancy and energization.

evidence.note: October 2024 expectation that occupancy begins in 1H 2025. This is a different milestone from the Q1 GPU target.
March 2025 update keeps 1H 2025 energization. No GPU count is reported, so the GPU milestone cannot be compared.

reviews.rationale: The claimed Q1 2025 target of 50,000 Blackwell chips and the revised rollout could not be verified from readable sources. The building schedules in the packet concern different milestones and show no slip. The evidence does not settle the claim.

semantics.note: 'I see no way' is a firm forecast that OpenAI cannot keep raising about $40B a year. 'Even if' is a concession, not an antecedent, and the for-profit clause is kept as description.

contract.note: The context says OpenAI needs 'another $40 billion in the next year'. Treating a further ≥$40B of completed primary funding within 12 months as a counterexample to 'no way' is a fair plain reading.

evidence.note: SoftBank disclosure: a $30B follow-on, separate from the March 2025 round, was completed in tranches from April to October 1, 2026.
Amazon 10-Q (unaudited): $13.7B in OpenAI preferred stock in Q2 2026, plus more investments. Combined with e1, completed funding exceeds $40B within 2026.

reviews.rationale: Investor disclosures show at least $43.7B of completed new primary investment in OpenAI between April and October 1, 2026, which is within a 12-month interval and excludes the original round. That meets the contract's early-resolution rule, so the forecast is contradicted.
